beginner.stem: How many protons does a Rubidium atom have? (That number is also its place on the table.)
beginner.explanation: Rubidium is element 37. A neutral atom has 37 protons and 37 electrons.

beginner.stem: What is the chemical symbol for Rubidium?
beginner.explanation: The catalog writes Rubidium as Rb.

beginner.stem: Which element has the symbol Rb?
beginner.explanation: Rb is Rubidium, atomic number 37.

beginner.stem: Which column of the table holds Rubidium? (Columns are called groups.)
beginner.explanation: Rubidium is in group 1.

beginner.stem: Which block of the table contains Rubidium? (Blocks are s, p, d, or f.)

beginner.stem: What kind of element is Rubidium on this table?

beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Rubidium?
options: In 1766 Henry Cavendish collected a gas from metals and acids and called it inflammable air.
Johan August Arfwedson found a new alkali in the mineral petalite in 1817, working in Berzelius’s laboratory.

beginner.stem: How does the catalog describe the discovery of Rubidium?

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Rubidium in this catalog?

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Rubidium in this catalog?

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Rubidium in this catalog?
options: A Metal That Will Not Wait
beginner.explanation: Rubidium sits below potassium among the alkali metals, and moist air or a drop of water is enough to show why it is stored with care.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Rubidium in this catalog?
